headline: Strong multi-firm audit coverage and public source repos at pinned SHAs, but no deployed contract addresses discovered — bytecode verification status on block explorers cannot be confirmed this run.

findings.text: No deployed contract addresses for Grove Finance (grove-labs) were discovered in this run. The address_book is null, the grove-address-registry GitHub repo was inaccessible, and Etherscan search returned only unrelated tokens named 'GROVE'. Bytecode verification status cannot be confirmed for any contract on any supported chain.

A public GitHub organisation (github.com/grove-labs) exists with 7 AGPL-3.0 Solidity repositories: grove-alm-controller, grove-spells, grove-address-registry, dss-allocator, grove-gov-relay, xchain-helpers, endgame-toolkit. Repos are public and contain Solidity source. No deploy-commit SHA or bytecode match was confirmed because no deployed addresses are known this run; source-to-deployed correspondence is recorded as an unknowns item.

The Protocol Security docs page lists audits for each major component at pinned commit SHAs: ALM Controller v1.6.0 (Spearbit/Cantina + ChainSecurity) and v1.8.0 (Certora + ChainSecurity); Gov Relay v1.1.0 (Spearbit/Cantina) and v1.2.0 (Certora + ChainSecurity); X-Chain Helpers v1.1.0 (Spearbit/Cantina + ChainSecurity) and v1.2.0 (Certora + ChainSecurity); Token Contract (ChainSecurity + Cantina, via endgame-toolkit). Audit PDF for v1.8.0 ChainSecurity confirmed as a 711 KB file at commit 36bf0fc. Audit dates were not extractable from fetched pages (PDFs not rendered); no staleness determination was possible.

Audit firms are ChainSecurity, Spearbit (via Cantina platform), and Certora — all broadly recognized in the Solidity security community. Certora is specifically noted for formal verification rather than traditional auditing, and is listed in the recognized-firm set.

Post-audit drift cannot be assessed: no deployed addresses were found to compare against audited repo commits, and the PDFs were not rendered to extract audited commit SHAs or dates. Recorded as unknowns.

Proxy/implementation verification status cannot be assessed without deployed addresses. The grove-alm-controller repo description references ALMProxy as the custody layer, which may be a proxy pattern. Cannot confirm whether proxy and implementation are both verified on-chain.

steelman.red: No deployed contract addresses were discovered, so it is impossible to confirm that any bytecode is verified on any block explorer; if the contracts are unverified, users cannot independently inspect what code is running.
steelman.orange: Public source repos and multi-firm, multi-round audits (ChainSecurity, Spearbit, Certora) at pinned commit SHAs provide strong off-chain verifiability evidence, but on-chain bytecode verification could not be confirmed this run due to absent address discovery, placing the overall posture between green and red.
steelman.green: The protocol employs a documented multi-layered audit strategy requiring at least two independent audit rounds per major version from recognized firms, with formal verification via Certora, and public AGPL-3.0 source repos at pinned SHAs — meeting the spirit of green verifiability even if on-chain verification was not confirmed this run.

rationale.verdict: Choosing orange because the off-chain verifiability signals (recognized-firm audits at pinned SHAs, public source repos) are clearly present and exceed the red threshold, but on-chain bytecode verification — a required green condition per the grading rubric — cannot be confirmed in this run due to the complete absence of discovered deployed addresses on any supported chain. The orange steelman accurately captures the mixed posture: strong audit hygiene, unresolved on-chain confirmation.

protocol_metadata.about: Grove Finance is an institutional-grade onchain credit protocol that routes USDS stablecoin liquidity into diversified credit strategies across multiple chains (Ethereum, Base, Plume, Avalanche). It operates within the Sky Ecosystem as a capital allocation layer, using vault-based, non-custodial infrastructure (ALMProxy + Controllers + RateLimits) to connect DeFi with real-world credit markets and institutional asset managers. Grove is developed by Grove Labs, a subsidiary of Steakhouse Financial, and was incubated under Sky's Endgame architecture.
